sonnet.problem: Card 11 only says the part is heavy and what the scribes do 'to people'. It never says who they hurt, so nothing lets the baker tell widows from orphans. Card 12 is a coin flip, and card 11 tells nothing of verse 40's content.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answers 'A double blessing' and 'A great reward' reuse 'blessing' and 'reward', which were already shown as wrong answers on card 13.
sonnet.rule: An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The right answer, 'how can He be David's son', repeats the 'Son of David' fact already shown as the right answer on card 2. Card 5 has also just set up the exact contradiction, so this mostly re-asks a known point.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact.

sonnet.problem: Card 20 asks about the same surplus-versus-poverty contrast in verse 44 that card 19 already asks about, and card 19's question and answer already cover it.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.
